newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela says Mobutu studying peace plan.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela says Mobutu studying peace plan.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday that Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko was studying South African proposals to end Zaire's civil war and had promised to respond to them by Monday.
"We are confident we are making progress," Mandela told a news conference after two-and-a-half hour talks with Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila. "Matters are going to plan."

Kabila told the news conference: "We shall wait until Monday to receive another answer from the Mobutu side." Asked if he would halt his rebel advance on the capital Kinshasa, Kabila said: "I have nothing to say about it."
Mandela has tabled a two-page proposal for a transition to democracy in Zaire after 32 years of Mobutu's autocratic rule.
In Kinshasa "bloodbath" was a word on many lips as the teeming capital of five million people prepared for the worst.

Mandela, bidding to rescue Zairean peace talks, sent a jet to the Angolan enclave of Cabinda to fetch the rebel leader, who on Wednesday refused at the last minute to meet Mobutu on a South African ship, citing security fears.
